page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-64 is a compute-optimized server instance built on the ARM64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There are no bundled GPUs or local NVMe storage drives included with this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory throughput. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 116240.18 and a top-tier passmark memory score of 3299.87. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 7912.85 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and 190.24 GB/sec for uncached large block writes. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 719.88 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier of tested configurations.

This instance is highly optimized for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and parallel processing, such as database operations, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference. It demonstrated 134.13 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 123.05 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators limits its applicability for heavy deep learning training or storage-intensive database clusters requiring local NVMe disks.
